react_result.final_narrative_text: This metabolomics differential set is dominated by tryptophan metabolism, which achieves cross-paradigm consensus across three independent analytical paradigms: over-representation analysis (RaMP multi-DB, FDR 1.08e-15; MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, raw p 1.79e-07) and m/z-direct activity scoring (Mummichog, p 8.40e-05). Six of the eight input metabolites — L-tryptophan, tryptamine, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and quinolinic acid — map directly to the KEGG tryptophan degradation pathway (KEGG:hsa00380). A seventh node, L-proline, maps instead to the arginine and proline metabolism pathway, reflecting its independent metabolic pool. The tryptophan signal branches along two functionally distinct axes: the biogenic-amine arm (tryptamine → serotonin → melatonin, captured by Reactome R-HSA-209931 Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis, FDR 1.39e-08) and the kynurenine-to-NAD+ arm (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid → quinolinic acid → nicotinamide), which appears in both the niacin/nicotinamide metabolism pathway (KEGG:hsa00760) and the WikiPathways NAD+ biosynthetic routes. Driver-metabolite analysis identifies serotonin (KEGG:C00780) as the single most-connected node: it participates in both the biogenic-amine branch and the NAD+ branch indirectly, and it is the only compound confirmed in three independent pathway hits. The treatment group perturbation is consistent with coordinated upregulation or accumulation of the tryptophan→serotonin→melatonin axis alongside activation of the immunologically relevant kynurenine arm, suggesting a phenotype characterized by simultaneous neurochemical and redox/metabolic reprogramming.

RaMP multi-DB ORA returned tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:map00380) as the top hit with FDR 1.08e-15 and six metabolites: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and quinolinic acid. The converging evidence across ORA, network-activity, and m/z-direct paradigms points to a treatment-induced reprogramming of tryptophan catabolism spanning both the neuroactive biogenic-amine branch and the immunologically relevant kynurenine branch.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis identified tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway across three independent methods. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as the top hit with FDR 1.08e-15 and six overlapping metabolites: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and quinolinic acid. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently returned KEGG:hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as rank 1 with p 1.79e-07 and five overlapping metabolites: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and tryptamine. Mummichog m/z-direct activity returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as the top pathway with p 8.40e-05 and thirteen overlapping metabolites including L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and tryptamine. These three concordant results establish tryptophan metabolism as the primary biological pathway affected by treatment. The downstream branch Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) was also identified by RaMP ORA as rank 8, confirming the neuroactive arm of tryptophan catabolism. The kynurenine arm leading to NAD+ biosynthesis (WP:WP4210) appears at RaMP rank 2 (FDR 6.01e-11), represented by quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. Cross-paradigm consensus across ORA, network-activity, and m/z-direct paradigms converges on treatment-induced reprogramming of tryptophan catabolism.
